subtitle: How a hill chief in shadow raised a banner that outlived empires

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a rugged Vindhyan hilltop at dusk
panels.action: Nannuka stands on a rocky outcrop above dense forest, planting a tall spear with a crescent-like banner into the wind as a faint moon rises behind him over the Bundelkhand hills.

dialogue.text: Centuries before Khajuraho’s carved gods, a near-forgotten hill chief named Nannuka planted a moon-banner in Pratihara shadow—and quietly began a kingdom.

i18n.hi: खजुराहो की तराशी देव-मूर्तियों से सदियों पहले, नन्नुका नाम का लगभग भूला पहाड़ी सरदार प्रतिहारों की छाया में चाँद-ध्वज गाड़कर चुपचाप एक राज्य बुनने लगा।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over a patchwork of forests, rocky hills and scattered villages
panels.action: A wide landscape of Bundelkhand in the early 9th century, scrub forests and rivers threading through rocky Vindhyan ridges, with smoke rising from small settlements and a faint stone shrine among trees.

dialogue.text: Long before anyone spoke of Chandellas or Khajuraho, the Vindhyan uplands of Bundelkhand were a mosaic of forests, shrines and small chiefships, known to distant courts as Jijhoti.

i18n.hi: चंदेल या खजुराहो का नाम दूर था, तब बूँदेलखंड के विन्ध्य पठार जंगलों, देवस्थानों और छोटे सरदारों की जाल-बुनावट थे, जिन्हें दूर के दरबार ‘जिझोति’ कहते थे।

panels.action: A ghostly image of the monk Xuanzang rides a mule past a distant hill-temple as village folk and ascetics move around, the scene hazy as if recalled from an old memory.

dialogue.text: The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang, passing here in the 7th century, wrote of a land called Chih-chi-to, dotted with monasteries and Brahminical shrines—already a sacred landscape before Nannuka’s time.

i18n.hi: सातवीं सदी में निकले चीनी यात्री श्वानत्सांग ने यहाँ से गुजरते हुए चिह-ची-तो नाम के देश का ज़िक्र किया—जहाँ मठों और ब्राह्मण देवालयों से भरा पवित्र भू-दृश्य था, नन्नुका से बहुत पहले से।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a stylised Pratihara court scene
panels.action: In a dim palace hall, a Pratihara maharaja sits on a modest throne, generals and feudatory chiefs standing in attendance, a large map of central India marked with tiny banners behind them.

dialogue.text: By the early 800s, the Gurjara-Pratiharas stretched their hand over this region, ruling through local feudatories who guarded hill-passes, river fords, and shrines in the Vindhyas.

i18n.hi: आठवीं सदी के शुरू में ही गुर्जर-प्रतिहारों ने इस भूभाग पर हाथ फैला दिया, और विन्ध्य पहाड़ियों में घाट, नदी-घाट और देवस्थानों की रखवाली करते हुए स्थानीय सामंतों से राज करवाया।

panels.action: Nannuka stands in a simple audience chamber carved from stone, wearing a plain warrior’s tunic and a modest torque, head slightly bowed yet eyes steady as he receives a small Pratihara emblem.

dialogue.text: Later inscriptions remember Nannuka as one such chief—a Pratihara feudatory in the Vindhyan uplands, holding a modest seat that later ages would call Jejakabhukti.

i18n.hi: बाद की अभिलेखों में नन्नुका को ऐसे ही एक सरदार के रूप में याद किया गया—विन्ध्य के ऊपरी भाग का प्रतिहार सामंत, जिसकी साधारण गद्दी को आगे चलकर ‘जेझकभुक्ति’ कहा गया।

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot in an open courtyard
panels.action: In a stone courtyard open to the sky, Nannuka conducts a small council with grey-bearded elders and younger warriors; behind them, women draw water and children play near a shrine.

dialogue.text: His world was not yet imperial. It was a cluster of villages, hill-forts and fields, where a chief sheltered his people, sent levies to his suzerain, and slowly wove his own authority.

i18n.hi: उसकी दुनिया अभी साम्राज्य नहीं थी। बस गाँवों, पहाड़ी किलों और खेतों का झुंड था, जहाँ सरदार अपने लोगों को ढालता, अपने स्वामी को सेना भेजता और धीरे-धीरे अपनी ही हुकूमत बुनता।

panels.shot: wide shot of a rugged frontier post
panels.action: On a rocky ridge, Nannuka oversees men reinforcing a stockade, carts bringing stone and timber; below, a winding track leads to a forested valley with glimpses of scattered huts and a small temple.

dialogue.text: Recent historians see his rise as part of a slow state-forming—the tightening of control over grazing lands, trade paths and shrine sites, not a sudden empire born in a single battle.

i18n.hi: नए इतिहासकार उसकी उभरती ताकत को धीरे-धीरे बनती रियासत मानते हैं—चराई-ज़मीन, व्यापार-पथ और देवस्थानों पर कसती पकड़, न कि किसी एक युद्ध से अचानक पैदा हुआ साम्राज्य।

panels.shot: evening wide shot with campfire glow
panels.action: Night in the camp: Nannuka sits by a small fire under the stars, listening as a wandering bard dramatically recounts a tale of a child born from the moon to a forest woman.

dialogue.text: But stories did not wait. Around many fires, bards sang of kings sprung from gods and moons. In time, later poets would wrap Nannuka’s house in such silvered legend.

i18n.hi: पर कहानियाँ इंतज़ार कहाँ करती हैं। अलावों के पास कई जगह भाट देवों और चाँद से निकले राजाओं के गीत गाने लगे; समय के साथ कवियों ने नन्नुका के घर को भी ऐसे चाँदीले किस्सों में लपेट दिया।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Nannuka’s thoughtful face lit by firelight
panels.action: Nannuka’s weathered face, lit by the flicker of the campfire, shows quiet focus; his hand rests on the hilt of his sword while his gaze drifts toward the dark silhouette of a hill-temple.

dialogue.speaker: nannuka
dialogue.text: Let tales be for the poets. I must make this land hold together.

i18n.hi: कथा कवियों के लिए रहने दो; मुझे तो इस धरती को ही जोड़े रखना है।

panels.shot: mid-distance shot at a local shrine
panels.action: At a small stone shrine under a large tree, Nannuka stands beside priests and local headsmen as a simple ritual is performed; villagers watch, some bowing, others whispering among themselves.

dialogue.text: He moved by weaving himself into the sacred landscape—patron of a shrine here, protector of a fair there—tying hill and village to his name as firmly as to his overlord’s.

i18n.hi: वह धीरे-धीरे खुद को इस पवित्र भू-दृश्य में पिरोने लगा—कहीं किसी देवस्थान का संरक्षक, कहीं मेले का रखवाला—और पहाड़-गाँव दोनों को अपने नाम से उतना ही बाँधने लगा जितना अपने स्वामी से।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot near a fortified gateway
panels.action: At the gate of a small hill-fort, Nannuka watches as a Pratihara messenger arrives on horseback; behind him his retainers look on, some tense, some curious, as a banner bearing the Pratihara emblem flutters.

dialogue.text: The Pratihara world itself was shifting, pressured on many fronts. In such times, frontier chiefs could either shrink into obscurity, or begin to act as more than obedient vassals.

i18n.hi: खुद प्रतिहारों की दुनिया भी कई मोर्चों से हिल रही थी; ऐसे समयों में सरहद के सरदार या तो सिमटकर गुम हो जाते, या फिर आज्ञाकारी जागीरदार से बढ़कर खेलना शुरू करते।

panels.action: Inside a simple hall, Nannuka stands over a low map scratched into sand, moving pebbles that mark villages and routes, while a trusted adviser speaks softly beside him.

dialogue.text: The Khajuraho prashastis, though written much later, remember him not as a shadow, but as a beginning—the founder from whom a line of chiefs and then kings would claim descent.

i18n.hi: खजुराहो के प्रशस्ति-शिलालेख, भले बाद में लिखे गए, उसे परछाईं नहीं, शुरुआत मानते हैं—वही संस्थापक, जिससे सरदारों और फिर राजाओं की वंशरेखा खुद को जोड़ती है।

panels.shot: symbolic low-angle shot on a hilltop
panels.action: On a bare hill overlooking forest and fields, Nannuka raises a new standard bearing a simple crescent motif; a handful of warriors and villagers stand behind him as the wind pulls the cloth taut.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions do not show the day he “planted” his own banner. Yet between the lines, we see a modest act of claiming—a hill, a cluster of villages, a name that would endure.

i18n.hi: अभिलेख यह नहीं बताते कि उसने अपना ध्वज किस दिन ‘गाड़ा’; पर पंक्तियों के बीच एक साधारण दावा दिखता है—एक पहाड़ी, कुछ गाँव, और एक नाम जो टिककर रह गया।

panels.action: A mason in a later century chisels sharp Nagari letters into stone; the camera lingers on the words naming Nannuka-deva as founder, dust rising as the chisel strikes.

dialogue.text: Many years after his death, scribes at Khajuraho carved his memory into stone, calling him Nannuka-deva and tracing a genealogy back to his modest seat in the forests of Jijhoti.

i18n.hi: उसकी मौत के बरसों बाद खजुराहो के शिल्पियों ने पत्थर पर उसकी याद उकेरी, उसे ‘नन्नुका-देव’ कहा और वंशावली को जिझोति के जंगलों में उसकी साधारण गद्दी तक खींच ले गए।

panels.action: On one side, a court poet performs before a later Chandela king, reciting a fanciful scene of a moon-beam descending on a riverbank woman; on the other, the sober inscription stone stands in temple light.

dialogue.text: By then, new stories had grown. Poets told of Hemavati and Chandravarman, of moon-born kings. Yet the Khajuraho stones are silent on these tales, remembering instead only a human founder.

i18n.hi: तब तक नई कहानियाँ उग आई थीं। कवि हेमावती और चंद्रवर्मन, चाँद-जन्मे राजाओं की गाथाएँ गाने लगे; पर खजुराहो की चट्टानें इन किस्सों पर चुप रहीं, और बस एक मानवीय संस्थापक को ही याद रख पाईं।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of Khajuraho evolving
panels.action: A sweeping view shows the site of Khajuraho changing over time: first a forested ridge, then small shrines, then grand rising temples alive with sculptors and pilgrims, clouds racing overhead to suggest centuries.

dialogue.text: From Nannuka’s compact domain, his descendants would raise the famed temples of Khajuraho, layering stone upon stone on ground that had been sacred since Xuanzang’s time and before.

i18n.hi: नन्नुका की छोटी सी रियासत से ही उसके वंशज खजुराहो के मशहूर मंदिर उठाएँगे, पत्थर पर पत्थर चढ़ाकर उसी धरती पर, जो श्वानत्सांग के समय से भी पवित्र मानी जाती थी।

panels.action: Nannuka’s figure appears faintly, almost like a memory, over the backdrop of Khajuraho’s later temples, his face calm, watching the bustling pilgrims and the intricate carvings below.

dialogue.text: He never saw these towers or heard the full weight of the name Chandella. His work was quieter: stitching a frontier into a polity that others would adorn.

i18n.hi: वह न इन शिखरों को देख पाया, न ‘चंदेल’ नाम का पूरा भार सुन पाया; उसका काम सादा था—सीमांत को जोड़कर ऐसा गणराज्य बुनना, जिसे आगे आने वाले सजाएँगे।

panels.shot: closing contemplative wide over ruins and sky
panels.action: Modern ruins of Khajuraho’s outskirts and the rugged Bundelkhand landscape are seen at sunset, old stone and living village blending as a pale moon rises over the Vindhyan horizon.

dialogue.text: In the end, Nannuka’s real legacy lies where inscription and legend meet—reminding us that lasting kingdoms are built in earth and stone, while their glories travel on the breath of myth.

i18n.hi: अंततः नन्नुका की असली धरोहर वहीं है जहाँ अभिलेख और किंवदंती मिलते हैं—याद दिलाते हुए कि टिकाऊ राज्य मिट्टी और पत्थर में बनते हैं, और उनकी महिमा हवाओं में उड़ती मिथक बन जाती है।

title_i18n.hi: नन्नुका ने गाड़ा चाँद का ध्वज

subtitle_i18n.en: How a hill chief in shadow raised a banner that outlived empires
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे छाया में बैठे पहाड़ी सरदार ने उठाया ऐसा झंडा जो सल्तनतों से भी लंबा जीया
